reason: The text explicitly names only three individual characters: Moses (מֹשֶׁה), Aaron (אַהֲרֹן), and Pharaoh (פַּרְעֹה). All three are unambiguously leaders—Moses as God's prophet and leader of the Israelites, Aaron as his brother and priestly leader, and Pharaoh as the ruler of Egypt. Other groups mentioned (the magicians/sorcerers, servants, the people of Egypt and Israel) are referred to collectively by their role or status, not by personal names. There are no named characters in subordinate positions.
